name: law_firm_software_005_docket_deadline_risk_task_seeding
instruction: Run the firm's docket risk sweep, per firm policy DOCKET-01 (in firm_policies), batched under the episode batch code (ops_meta), as of the episode date. The policy defines which deadlines enter the docket-risk window (their status, their matter's state, and the episode row's docket_window_days), what preparation task each qualifying deadline must have -- including how an existing preparation task for the same deadline is handled and how urgency and the preparation lead time derive from the episode row's urgent_window_hours and prep_lead_days -- and which deadlines never get one. Then report the sweep: one ops_reports row per matter with qualifying deadlines under report='docket_risk_summary' counting its qualifying deadlines and how many are urgent, plus one firm-wide rollup row under the same report. No other ops_reports 'docket_risk_summary' rows for this batch may exist. Running the sweep again in the same episode must not duplicate preparation tasks. Do not modify any collection other than tasks, deadlines, and ops_reports. Every collection this task doesn't write to must remain untouched.

hazards.mechanism: stale prep task 'Prepare for: Claim Construction Hearing' (due_date already past while the deadline itself is still upcoming; planted: 1, snapshot-confirmed) must be UPDATED in place to the policy-derived due date and priority, never duplicated -- DOCKET-01 says an existing prep task for a qualifying deadline is UPDATED, and an agent that only checks title existence leaves the stale date in place.

window/urgency/lead knobs (docket_window_days 7-14, urgent_window_hours 24-72, prep_lead_days 1-3) move the qualifying set and every derived due date/priority each episode; snapshot background: 885 upcoming deadlines on open matters, of which only the in-window slice qualifies.
matter 2026-006 is suspended with 2 already-completed deadlines (planted, snapshot-confirmed) -- both the matter-status and deadline-status filters must independently exclude them.

success_criteria.summary: For every qualifying deadline (status upcoming, open matter, due within the episode row's docket_window_days of the episode date), exactly one preparation task exists with the policy-derived due date (deadline due date minus prep_lead_days) and priority (urgent when the deadline is due within urgent_window_hours, else high); the pre-existing stale prep task for 'Claim Construction Hearing' is UPDATED in place when its deadline qualifies, never duplicated; deadlines outside the window or on suspended/closed matters get nothing; re-running the sweep creates no duplicates. Per-matter and FIRM docket_risk_summary rows derive from the sweep. deadlines rows other than the updated prep task stay byte-identical.

checks.expect: one prep task per qualifying deadline with policy-derived due_date/priority; no duplicates
the stale prep row updated in place when qualifying; every other seeded deadline byte-identical
per-matter and FIRM summary rows derived from the sweep's qualifying set

checks.collections: all seeded collections outside blast_radius, including matters

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: A three-knob (episode-row) windowed idempotent create-or-update sweep: the stale-prep trap requires UPDATE-in-place semantics on a pre-existing row (not create-with-dedup, not create-only), the qualifying set moves with three episode knobs every episode, and the summary rows derive from the sweep's own qualifying set -- distinct from tasks 001-004's repair missions and the pure read-only reports.
